Intheliterature,therearetwosimilarbutdistinctnotionsofatoroidal3-manifolds:homotopi- cally atoroidal and geometrically atoroidal. A manifold is geometrically atoroidal if every embedded torus with injective π1 in M is isotopic to a component of ∂M. In contrast, a manifold is homotopi- cally atoroidal if every immersed torus, including those with self-intersections, with injective π1 is homotopic to a component of ∂M. The definition of homotopically atoroidal implies geometrically atoroidal, but the converse does not hold. There are irreducible geometrically atoroidal 3-manifolds M that satisfy Z × Z ⊂π1(M), where the Z × Z factor is carried by an immersed torus that cannot be homotoped to ∂M. Notable examples include Σ0,3×S1 (the product of a 3-punctured sphere with S1), and the complement in S3 of any torus knot. See e.g. [91] for more details.
For this one formally uses the sphere theorem of 3-manifolds, saying that any element of π2(M) may always be represented as a properly embedded sphere.
